title: What does the XRPL GlobalFreeze account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of GlobalFreeze and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, GlobalFreeze freezes an issuer's trust-line tokens according to XRPL's freeze rules. [1]

It concerns assets issued by the account, not the XRP balances of everyone connected to it. Freezing differs from clawback: restricting movement is not the same as reclaiming a balance. Interactions with NoFreeze and individual line settings matter. Inspect issuer and line state before interpreting a failed transfer as proof that a holder has no funds. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for GlobalFreeze and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why GlobalFreeze is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
